thread:
maria.g: FYI canary promotion is blocked — deploybot is failing prefetch of the artifact index for today
alex.t: error messages? service or CI?
maria.g: CI job shows 404s from artifact-store when deploybot asks for index v2025-03-15. suspect TTL/stale index pointer
samir: I saw a couple of 'cache-miss' spikes earlier. Could be the index rotation job and the cache expirer ran at the same minute
deploy-bot: automated: prefetch failed: GET /artifacts/index/v2025-03-15 -> 404 (x-request-id=abcd-1234)
alex.t: can you paste the CI log snippet?
maria.g: sure — trimmed: ```
[2025-03-15T14:02:09Z] deploybot.prefetch index=v2025-03-15
[2025-03-15T14:02:10Z] GET https://artifact-store/internal/artifacts/index/v2025-03-15 -> 404
[2025-03-15T14:02:11Z] error: index not found, aborting canary promote
```
release-ops: tagging in. Did we run the index-rotation earlier today?
samir: rotation ran at 14:00, index v2025-03-15 was promoted and a tombstone written for legacy pointer. TTL eviction ran at 14:01 due to a bug in the expirer (double-delete race)
alex.t: double-delete? so the pointer was removed then tombstoned then expirer cleaned it up too aggressively?
samir: exactly. The artifact-store GC treated the tombstone as stale metadata and deleted actual index blob. We have no replica for that short window
maria.g: consequence: deploybot can't fetch prefetch manifest -> canary tasks fail -> promotion blocked. We need a decision: roll back canary, pin to previous index, or manual artifact restore
release-ops: what's the fastest unblocking option?
samir: fastest is to restore the index from object-store backup (snapshots every 6h). Recovery ~15-20m; manual pin is immediate but requires force-promote against older index (risking missing last config). Rollback isn't ideal because canary already has partial runs
alex.t: can we temporarily bypass prefetch and let canary use lazy fetch? deploybot supports a --lazy-fetch flag but changes behavior and needs approval for release policy
maria.g: approving lazy-fetch would bypass the prefetch guard — riskier. Ops prefers restore to preserve guarantees
release-ops: agreed. start restore, notify SREs, and hold promotion until validated. Also add a release note to the ticket and ping customers on the change window if it slips
samir: kicking off restore now. ETA 18m. I'll monitor integrity checks.
maria.g: thx. will add to release ticket and block promotion in the console (pin: hold-promote=true)
release-ops: also: we should consider a short-term mitigation: increase tombstone retention so tombstones aren't GC'd for 30m after rotation. Samir can you open an infra PR?
samir: on it. will target canary ASAP and schedule postmortem
alex.t: if restore fails, we do forced-promote to v2025-03-14 with document in the changelog. But let's not preempt the restore
deploy-bot: automated: promotion blocked (reason: prefetch index missing). Action required: manual unblock or retry after artifact restore
maria.g: updates will follow in thread. tagging @eng-oncall if needed :bell:
samir: restore completed, integrity check passed. I re-run a dry-prefetch against restored index -> 200 OK
release-ops: running a smoke promote in staged environment now
maria.g: smoke passed. unblocking promotion in console and proceeding with canary resume. noted for postmortem: expirer race + tombstone retention + replica policy
alex.t: add a short blurb to release notes: "Promotion briefly delayed due to artifact-index GC race; no customer impact. Fixes: tombstone retention bump and artifact-store replica hardening."
release-ops: change window unchanged. closing block. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
